0.0.n: A polite way to address a group, with さん adding respect.

0.1.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.3.n: Combines with 教師 to specify the language she teaches.

0.4.n: Used here as a job title before the speaker’s name.

0.5.n: Links the job title to the name, identifying Mirai as a Japanese teacher rather than expressing possession.

0.6.n: This is the speaker’s name, not the ordinary word for future.

0.7.n: Politely completes the introduction; the speaker leaves out 私, meaning I.

1.0.n: Sets the time for the proposed study session.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, telling us what time the sentence is about.

1.2.n: Pairs with に to describe studying with the speaker.

1.3.n: Turns 一緒 into a phrase describing how the studying will happen.

1.4.n: A noun linked by の to とき to describe a travel situation.

1.5.n: Connects 旅行 to とき, making the phrase refer to the time of a trip.

1.6.n: With 旅行の, it refers to occasions when you are traveling.

1.7.n: Marks 旅行のとき as the time when the Japanese is used.

1.8.n: The plain form comes before 日本語 to describe which Japanese expressions they will study.

1.9.n: Here it refers to Japanese expressions useful for travel.

1.10.n: Marks 日本語 as what they will study.

1.11.n: 勉強する becomes 勉強しましょう, a polite invitation to study together.

0.lit: Everyone, hello; Japanese-language teacher Mirai am.
0.tip: In introductions, a job title plus の plus a name identifies the person’s role.

1.lit: Today, as for, together, travel’s time during use Japanese, let’s study.
1.tip: 一緒に describes studying together, not traveling together.
